questions.stem: Bromomethane is treated with sodium metal in dry ether. The main organic product is
questions.explanation: This is the Wurtz reaction. Two molecules of the alkyl halide couple in the presence of sodium in dry ether, joining their alkyl groups: $2\,\mathrm{CH_3Br} + 2\,\mathrm{Na} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_3} + 2\,\mathrm{NaBr}$. The product has double the number of carbons of the halide.

optionRationale.1: Methane would need reduction without coupling.
optionRationale.2: Propane would form by coupling of CH$_3$ with a two-carbon unit.
optionRationale.4: Ethene would need elimination, which is not possible from a one-carbon halide.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is chiral?
questions.explanation: 2-Bromobutane, CH$_3$CHBrCH$_2$CH$_3$, has a carbon bonded to four different groups: H, Br, CH$_3$ and C$_2$H$_5$. It is therefore chiral and optically active. In the other compounds no carbon has four different groups.

optionRationale.1: No carbon in 1-bromobutane has four different groups.
optionRationale.2: The C-2 of 2-bromopropane carries two identical methyl groups.
optionRationale.3: The central carbon of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane carries three identical methyl groups.

questions.stem: Chlorobenzene is nitrated with a mixture of concentrated nitric acid and sulphuric acid. The major product is
questions.explanation: Chlorine deactivates the ring by its -I effect, but its lone pairs donate by resonance and direct the electrophile to the ortho and para positions. The para isomer is formed in larger amount because of less steric hindrance, so 4-chloronitrobenzene is major.

optionRationale.2: Halogens are ortho and para directing, not meta directing.
optionRationale.3: The C-Cl bond is not replaced under these conditions.
optionRationale.4: Chlorine retains its place and only one nitro group is introduced in a mono-nitration.

questions.objective: Predict the nitration product of chlorobenzene

questions.stem: Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. The major product is
questions.explanation: In the presence of a peroxide the addition of HBr proceeds by a free radical path and gives the anti-Markovnikov product. The bromine radical adds to the terminal carbon to give the more stable secondary radical, so the product is 1-bromopropane.

optionRationale.1: 2-Bromopropane is the Markovnikov product obtained without a peroxide.
optionRationale.3: A second bromine is not added by HBr under these conditions.
optionRationale.4: No alcohol is formed because no water or hydroxide is present.

questions.objective: Apply the peroxide effect to HBr addition

questions.stem: Bromoethane is treated with magnesium in dry ether, and the product is then treated with water. The final organic product is
questions.explanation: Bromoethane and magnesium in dry ether form the Grignard reagent C$_2$H$_5$MgBr. Water protonates the carbanion-like carbon of the Grignard reagent: $\mathrm{C_2H_5MgBr} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_6} + \mathrm{Mg(OH)Br}$. The product is ethane.

optionRationale.1: Butane is the Wurtz coupling product, which needs sodium.
optionRationale.2: Ethanol would need a carbonyl or oxygen source, not water alone.
optionRationale.4: Ethene would need elimination, which does not occur.

questions.objective: Recall the reaction of Grignard reagents with water

questions.stem: A haloalkane X (C$_4$H$_9$Br) is optically active. On heating with alcoholic KOH it gives mainly an alkene Y. Identify X and Y.
questions.explanation: Among the isomers C$_4$H$_9$Br only 2-bromobutane has a chiral carbon. Alcoholic KOH causes dehydrohalogenation, and by Saytzeff's rule the more substituted alkene is the major product. This is but-2-ene, which is more stable than but-1-ene.

optionRationale.1: 1-Bromobutane has no chiral carbon, so it cannot be optically active.
optionRationale.2: The minor product but-1-ene would be favoured only against Saytzeff's rule.
optionRationale.3: 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane has no chiral carbon and gives an achiral alkene.

questions.stem: The dipole moment of chlorobenzene (1.69 D) is lower than that of cyclohexyl chloride (2.2 D). This is mainly because in chlorobenzene
options: the C-Cl carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised and more electronegative, and the lone pair on chlorine is delocalised into the ring
the C-Cl bond is longer and therefore weaker than in cyclohexyl chloride
chlorine is less electronegative when attached to a benzene ring
chlorobenzene molecules associate through hydrogen bonds
questions.explanation: An sp$^2$ carbon is more electronegative than an sp$^3$ carbon, so the C-Cl bond is less polar. Also the lone pair on chlorine takes part in resonance with the ring, moving some negative charge back towards the ring and reducing the dipole.

optionRationale.2: The C-Cl bond in chlorobenzene is shorter, not longer, because of partial double bond character.
optionRationale.3: The electronegativity of chlorine does not change with the group it is bonded to.
optionRationale.4: Chlorobenzene has no hydrogen bonding and no N-H or O-H groups.

questions.objective: Explain the low dipole moment of haloarenes

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Ethyl bromide reacts with KCN to give mainly ethyl cyanide, whereas with AgCN it gives mainly ethyl isocyanide.
Reason (R): KCN is predominantly covalent and AgCN is predominantly ionic.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: KCN is ionic and gives free cyanide ions, which attack through the carbon (the better nucleophilic site) to give the cyanide. AgCN is covalent, so only the lone pair on nitrogen is available and the isocyanide forms. The assertion is true but the reason reverses the nature of the two salts.

optionRationale.1: The reason is false, so it cannot explain the assertion.
optionRationale.2: The reason is false, not merely a weak explanation.
optionRationale.4: The assertion is true: the nature of the cyanide salt decides the product.

questions.objective: Explain the ambident nature of the cyanide ion

questions.stem: Match the compound in List-I with its type in List-II.
questions.explanation: In CH$_2$=CHCl the halogen is on a doubly bonded carbon, so it is a vinylic halide (A-III). In C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Cl the halogen is on a carbon next to the benzene ring, so it is benzylic (B-II). CH$_2$=CHCH$_2$Cl is allylic (C-I), and C$_6$H$_5$Cl has halogen on the ring, so it is an aryl halide (D-IV).

optionRationale.1: This code interchanges the matches of A and B; the correct pairs are A-III and B-II.
optionRationale.3: This code interchanges the matches of C and D; the correct pairs are C-I and D-IV.
optionRationale.4: This code interchanges the matches of A and C; the correct pairs are A-III and C-I.

questions.objective: Classify halides by the nature of the carbon bearing the halogen

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about haloalkanes.
A. For the same alkyl group the boiling points follow the order R-I > R-Br > R-Cl > R-F.
B. Among isomeric haloalkanes the boiling point decreases with increased branching.
C. The densities of haloalkanes increase in the order R-Cl < R-Br < R-I.
D. Haloalkanes dissolve readily in water.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Boiling point and density rise with the size and mass of the halogen, and branching lowers the boiling point by reducing the surface area. Haloalkanes are only slightly soluble in water because they cannot form hydrogen bonds to compensate for breaking water-water hydrogen bonds, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: D is wrong, and C is also correct.
optionRationale.2: D is wrong because haloalkanes are poorly soluble in water.
optionRationale.4: It includes the wrong statement D and omits the correct statements B and C.
